title.narrative: Access to quality essential lifesaving HEALTH and NUTRITION assistance for conflict-, drought- and flood-affected Rural communities in JAMMAME.

description.narrative: ltpgtSFH will provide integrated primary health care and nutrition services as defined in the Essential Package of Health Services 2020 guideline and in compliance with the Flagship allocation strategy. The services will be provided through 1 Fixed health Center and 1 Integrated mobile team linked to the fixed HC covering Singaleer, Farwamo and Towfiq sites. The proposed intervention will improve access to timely and quality essential health services by providing free treatment for communicable and non-communicable diseases, increasing access to routine childhood immunizations and as well as reproductive health services, care for injury and first aid, mental health and psychological support, and behavior change interventions at the household and community level to increase uptake of preventive services.ltbrgtSFH will focus on early diagnosis and treatment of common communicable diseases such as ARI, diarrhea, and malaria, improve routine immunization, uptake of PNC and ANC services and response to disease outbreaks. The clinical staff will use the Somalia National Treatment Guidelines for managing communicable diseases, as well as IMCI guidelines.ltbrgtTo ensure all children are protected against vaccine-preventable diseases, all children under the age of two who attend mobile outreaches will be screened for vaccination status screened and immunized in line with national routine immunization guidelines. SFH will continue to collaborate with MOH to ensure access to routine immunization at the outreach sites. SFH will obtain vaccines and Nutrition supplies through MOH/UNICEF.ltbrgtThe Integrated project will be headed by a Project manager supported by Health and Nutrition officers who is an experience clinician and trained public health practitioners. The Health officer be responsible for the coordination and implementation of the project in addition to handling complicated cases for referrals. The teams will have qualified health professionals that will include qualified nurses, auxiliary nurses, pharmacist, Team leaders/supervisors, screener, registrars and a health promoter. They will have a support team consisting of storekeeper, GBV/inclusion and HMIS officers. Each of the mobile teams will have a static/mobile tent and furniture (tables and chairs) that are collapsible and suitable for outreach services with an outreach van that will be hired and ensure the van hired have the capacity to carry both staffs and medical supplies. The mobile clinics will address the long distances to health facilities currently being traveled by women, men, boys and girls in rural areas.ltbrgtSFHI will also prioritize life-saving nutrition treatment targeting children under five years of age. SFH will implement Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) to manage SAM in children under 5 in line with national IMAM guidelines. Specific nutrition interventions will include community mobilization to increase access and coverage of CMAM services, early identification and referral of children aged 6-59 months with SAM treatment of SAM through OTP and referral of SAM with medical complications to the nearest Stabilization Centre. CHVs will undertake active case finding, defaulter/absentee tracing and home visits for children in the program with stagnant/recent loss of weight. This proposed nutrition intervention will be integrated into the primary health care services and WASH targeted facility, ensuring a comprehensive approach to addressing poor nutrition outcomes in communities.ltbrgtAid diversion is an ongoing concern for nutrition partners in Somalia. SFH will undertake robust measures to prevent and mitigate the diversion of nutrition supplies (misuse and sale) by implementing measures aligned with the Somalia Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) aid diversion action plan monitoring framework and the Nutrition Cluster’s recommendations. The national IMAM guideline admission criteria will be strictly adhered to, ensuring that only eligible beneficiaries receive treatment.ltbrgtlt/pgt
